140	/**
141	 * Build the remote script.
142	 *
143	 * Design rules, each of which the old one-liner broke:
144	 *
145	 *  - No `set -e` and no trailing `; true`. Control flow is explicit, and the exit
146	 *    status is irrelevant — the MARKERS are the contract, so a truncated or
147	 *    dropped connection is detectable (no `NXGU:END`) rather than indistinguishable
148	 *    from success.
149	 *  - steamcmd's own exit code is not trusted (it is famously unreliable and
150	 *    frequently non-zero on a perfectly good update). We match its own success
151	 *    line instead, and report the code alongside.
152	 *  - "no unit matched" is an outcome we emit, not a branch we swallow.
153	 *  - The post-restart state is polled and reported verbatim. `active` is the only
154	 *    thing that will be called success upstream.
155	 *
156	 * `family` is constrained to GAME_FAMILIES by the caller AND re-checked here, so
157	 * nothing unvalidated is interpolated into the shell.
158	 */
159	export function updateCommand(family: GameFamily): string {
160	  if (!GAME_FAMILIES.includes(family)) throw new Error(`not a game family: ${family}`);
161	  const appId = STEAM_APPID[family];
162	  const svc = SERVICE_HINT[family];
163	  // Both are compile-time constants from the tables above — never customer input.
164	
165	  // Emitted by every branch that must not go on to restart the service.
166	  const stopHere = [
167	    `st=$(systemctl is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null)`,
168	    `say "SKIPPED_RESTART:1"`,
169	    `say "STATE:${"$"}{st:-unknown}"`,
170	    `say "END"`,
171	    `exit 0`,
172	  ];
173	
174	  const steam = appId
175	    ? [
176	        `fresh=0`,
177	        `if command -v steamcmd >/dev/null 2>&1; then`,
178	        `  out=$(steamcmd +login anonymous +app_update ${appId} validate +quit 2>&1); rc=$?`,
179	        `  say "STEAM_RC:$rc"`,
180	        // steamcmd prints "Success! App '<id>' already up to date." when there was
181	        // nothing to download, and "Success! App '<id>' fully installed." when
182	        // there was. Both used to match one grep, so the two outcomes were
183	        // indistinguishable — see the CURRENT/OK split in the header note.
184	        `  if printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "Success! App '${appId}' already up to date"; then`,
185	        `    say "STEAM:CURRENT"`,
186	        `  elif printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "Success! App '${appId}'"; then`,
187	        `    fresh=1; say "STEAM:OK"`,
188	        `  else`,
189	        `    say "STEAM:FAIL"`,
190	        `    printf '%s' "$out" | grep -i 'error' | head -3 | while IFS= read -r l; do say "STEAM_ERR:$l"; done`,
191	        `  fi`,
192	        `else`,
193	        `  say "STEAM:ABSENT"`,
194	        `fi`,
195	        // Do NOT bounce a healthy game server for an update that did not happen:
196	        // a restart kicks every connected player off for nothing, and it would
197	        // make "the service was restarted" the only true half of a false claim.
198	        // This now also covers the "already up to date" case, which is the COMMON
199	        // one — it ran every 6 hours and disconnected everybody four times a day.
200	        `if [ "$fresh" != "1" ]; then`,
201	        ...stopHere.map((l) => `  ${l}`),
202	        `fi`,
203	      ].join("\n")
204	    : [
205	        // No update source exists for this family, so there is nothing a restart
206	        // could apply. Restarting anyway is a pure loss: every connected player
207	        // is disconnected, four times a day, forever, to change nothing. The
208	        // rule two paragraphs up applies here MOST, and used not to be applied
209	        // here at all.
210	        `say "STEAM:NA"`,
211	        ...stopHere,
212	      ].join("\n");

214	  return [
215	    `say() { printf 'NXGU:%s\\n' "$1"; }`,
216	    // 1. Resolve the unit. `systemctl cat` succeeds only for a unit that exists.
217	    `unit=""`,
218	    `for c in ${svc} ${svc}-server; do`,
219	    `  if systemctl cat "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; then unit="$c"; break; fi`,
220	    `done`,

229	    // 3. Restart, and report the real result of the restart call.
230	    `systemctl restart "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1; say "RESTART_RC:$?"`,
231	    // 4. Wait for it to settle. A game server can take a while to open its port,

236	    `  if [ "$st" = "active" ] || [ "$st" = "failed" ]; then break; fi`,
237	    `  i=$((i+1)); sleep ${RESTART_WAIT_SLEEP_S}`,
238	    `done`,
239	    `say "STATE:${"$"}{st:-unknown}"`,
240	    `say "END"`,

248	export type GameUpdateFacts = {
249	  /** The systemd unit the script acted on, or null when nothing matched. */
250	  unit: string | null;
251	  /** `systemctl is-active` before the restart. */
252	  wasActive: string;
253	  /** Exit code of `systemctl restart`, or null when it never ran. */
254	  restartRc: number | null;
255	  /** `systemctl is-active` after the restart, settled or timed out. */
256	  state: string;
257	  /**
258	   * "ok" = steamcmd downloaded a NEW build. "current" = it confirmed the server
259	   * was already up to date and downloaded nothing. Collapsing those two into one
260	   * value is what made "<game> updated on <host>" fire every 6 hours forever.
261	   */
262	  steam: "ok" | "current" | "failed" | "absent" | "na" | "unknown";
263	  steamRc: number | null;
264	  steamErrors: string[];
265	  /** Did the script run to completion? No END marker means we know nothing. */
266	  complete: boolean;
267	};
268	
269	export function parseGameUpdateOutput(out: string): GameUpdateFacts {
270	  const text = String(out ?? "");
271	  const one = (re: RegExp): string | null => re.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null;
272	
273	  const steamRaw = one(/^NXGU:STEAM:(\w+)$/m);
274	  const steam =
275	    steamRaw === "OK" ? "ok"
276	    : steamRaw === "CURRENT" ? "current"
277	    : steamRaw === "FAIL" ? "failed"
278	    : steamRaw === "ABSENT" ? "absent"
279	    : steamRaw === "NA" ? "na"
280	    : "unknown";
281	
282	  const rc = (re: RegExp): number | null => {
283	    const v = one(re);
284	    return v === null ? null : Number(v);
285	  };
286	
287	  const unitLine = one(/^NXGU:UNIT:(.+)$/m);
288	  const steamErrors: string[] = [];
289	  for (const m of text.matchAll(/^NXGU:STEAM_ERR:(.*)$/gm)) steamErrors.push(m[1].trim());
290	
291	  return {
292	    unit: unitLine === null || unitLine === "NONE" ? null : unitLine.trim(),
293	    wasActive: one(/^NXGU:WAS:(.*)$/m)?.trim() || "unknown",
294	    restartRc: rc(/^NXGU:RESTART_RC:(-?\d+)$/m),
295	    state: one(/^NXGU:STATE:(.*)$/m)?.trim() || "unknown",
296	    steam,
297	    steamRc: rc(/^NXGU:STEAM_RC:(-?\d+)$/m),
298	    steamErrors,
299	    complete: /^NXGU:END$/m.test(text),
300	  };
301	}

304	// The verdict
305	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

307	export type GameUpdateVerdict =
308	  | {
309	      ok: true;
310	      title: string;
311	      body: string;
312	      /**
313	       * Is this an EVENT worth interrupting the customer for?
314	       *
315	       * This runs unattended every 6 hours. `notifyFailureOnce` already exists
316	       * because "the customer would learn to ignore them — which is the same
317	       * outcome as not telling them"; the success path had no equivalent and
318	       * notified on every single pass, so a healthy server produced four
319	       * notifications a day, forever, all of them titled "<game> updated on
320	       * <host>" when nothing had been updated. Only a real, observed change is
321	       * an event.
322	       */
323	      notify: boolean;
324	    }
325	  | { ok: false; reason: string };
326	
327	/**
328	 * Turn observed facts into the one thing the customer is told.
329	 *
330	 * Every refusal names the reason AND the command to run, because "update failed"
331	 * on a game server six hours after the fact is useless without a next step.
332	 * Every success states precisely what was proven — including, for minecraft and
333	 * terraria, that no game update took place at all, because there is no update
334	 * source for those families and saying otherwise was the original lie.
335	 */
336	export function judgeGameUpdate(opts: {
337	  family: GameFamily;
338	  hostname: string;
339	  facts: GameUpdateFacts;
340	}): GameUpdateVerdict {
341	  const { family, hostname, facts: f } = opts;
342	  const appId = STEAM_APPID[family];
343	
344	  if (!f.complete) {
345	    return {
346	      ok: false,
347	      reason:
348	        `the update script did not run to completion on ${hostname} (no end marker), so nothing about ` +
349	        `this run can be verified — the connection may have dropped or the command timed out. ` +
350	        `Nothing is being claimed. Re-run it by hand: systemctl status <your ${family} unit>`,
351	    };
352	  }
353	
354	  if (!f.unit) {
355	    return {
356	      ok: false,
357	      reason:
358	        `no systemd service for ${family} was found on ${hostname}, so nothing was updated and ` +
359	        `nothing was restarted. Check what the server actually runs with: ` +
360	        `systemctl list-units --type=service | grep -i ${family}`,
361	    };
362	  }
363	
364	  if (appId && f.steam === "absent") {
365	    return {
366	      ok: false,
367	      reason:
368	        `steamcmd is not installed on ${hostname}, so the ${family} game files were NOT updated. ` +
369	        `Auto-update cannot work on this server until it is present: apt-get install -y steamcmd ` +
370	        `(or reinstall from the ${family} image).`,
371	    };
372	  }
373	
374	  if (appId && f.steam !== "ok" && f.steam !== "current") {
375	    const detail = f.steamErrors.length ? ` steamcmd said: ${f.steamErrors.slice(0, 3).join(" | ")}` : "";
376	    return {
377	      ok: false,
378	      reason:
379	        `steamcmd did not report a successful update of app ${appId} on ${hostname} ` +
380	        `(exit ${f.steamRc ?? "unknown"}), so the game files were not updated and the service was ` +
381	        `left alone.${detail} Re-run by hand: steamcmd +login anonymous +app_update ${appId} validate +quit`,
382	    };
383	  }
384	
385	  // Nothing was restarted on these paths, so the state we observed is simply the
386	  // state the server was already in — do not describe it as a restart outcome.
387	  const restarted = f.steam === "ok";
388	
389	  if (f.state !== "active") {
390	    return {
391	      ok: false,
392	      reason: restarted
393	        ? `${f.unit} on ${hostname} is "${f.state}" after the restart` +
394	          (f.restartRc !== null && f.restartRc !== 0 ? ` (systemctl restart exited ${f.restartRc})` : "") +
395	          `, so your game server is NOT running. It was "${f.wasActive}" before this ran. ` +
396	          `Diagnose with: systemctl status ${f.unit} ; journalctl -u ${f.unit} -n 50`
397	        : `${f.unit} on ${hostname} is "${f.state}" — your game server is NOT running. Nothing was ` +
398	          `updated or restarted by this check, so this is not something we just did to it. ` +
399	          `Diagnose with: systemctl status ${f.unit} ; journalctl -u ${f.unit} -n 50`,
400	    };
401	  }
402	
403	  if (f.steam === "ok") {
404	    return {
405	      ok: true,
406	      notify: true, // a new build really was downloaded and applied
407	      title: `${family} updated on ${hostname}`,
408	      body:
409	        `steamcmd downloaded a new build of app ${appId}, and ${f.unit} was restarted and is active again ` +
410	        `(verified with systemctl, not assumed from an exit code).`,
411	    };
412	  }
413	
414	  if (f.steam === "current") {
415	    return {
416	      ok: true,
417	      notify: false, // nothing happened; four of these a day is noise, not news
418	      title: `${family} on ${hostname} is already up to date`,
419	      body:
420	        `steamcmd confirmed app ${appId} is already up to date, so nothing was downloaded and ${f.unit} was ` +
421	        `NOT restarted — no players were disconnected. It is active.`,
422	    };
423	  }
424	
425	  // No update source exists for this family. Say that, rather than implying one —
426	  // and do not restart, which is all this job could otherwise do here.
427	  return {
428	    ok: true,
429	    notify: false,
430	    title: `${family} server checked on ${hostname}`,
431	    body:
432	      `${f.unit} is active (verified). ${family} has no automatic update source on Nxeon, so there was ` +
433	      `nothing to download and your server was NOT restarted — restarting it every few hours would ` +
434	      `disconnect your players to change nothing. Update the server files yourself when a new version ships.`,
435	  };

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker

# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),

PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2

**Root causes were different for each server, and neither was a false-positive verification bug:**

**suplosmp (bedrock)** — Not actually broken. The customer themselves issued a `GAME_POWER` "stop" via the dashboard at 2026-09-16 00:05:15 UTC (confirmed via `Job` table history: `stop` action, `status: DONE`) and never restarted it. Every subsequent GAME_UPDATE run (every ~1-6h) correctly reported the bedrock service as "inactive" — that's true, not a bug. The actual defect: `gameUpdateSweep()` only checks the VM's `Server.status` (which stays "RUNNING" — that field tracks the VM's own power, not the game service inside it) and `autoUpdate`, so it kept blindly re-enqueuing checks against a service the customer had deliberately turned off, generating a FAILED job on every single run for 28+ straight hours.

**projectzomboid-kc0kcr** — Genuinely broken, and NOT a verification-logic issue: the host's root disk is 100% full (`/dev/sda1 77G 77G 0 100% /`), so Docker cannot (re)mount the container's overlay filesystem (`no space left on device`), and `projectzomboid.service` is crash-looping (systemd restart counter at 9800+ and climbing). The job is correctly and honestly reporting instability.

**What I fixed (code-only, deployed through the full pipeline):**
- Added `eligibleForUpdateSweep()` to `/opt/nxeon/lib/game-update-verify.ts`: reads the `_serviceState` that `gamePower()` already persists onto `Server.gameConfig` after any explicit start/stop/restart action, and skips the sweep only when it's exactly `"inactive"` (a clean, customer-initiated stop). A crash (`"failed"`), a mid-restart (`"activating"`), or no recorded state at all are still checked normally — those are exactly what this job should keep catching.
- Wired it into `gameUpdateSweep()` in `/opt/nxeon/worker/game-update.ts`.
- Added 4 new unit tests to `/opt/nxeon/test/game-update.test.ts` (27/27 passing).
